Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our procurement and finance teams are trying to line up internal PO timing with your billing cadence. A few clarifying questions so we can process this without delay: 

- Which specific events trigger an invoice? Options we saw in the draft include: activation (onboarding complete), milestone billing (per commit tranche), monthly calendar billing against the minimum commit, or only on receipt of a PO. Please call out the primary trigger and any fallback.
- For multi-entity purchases (our US parent vs EU subsidiary), who is contractually responsible for VAT/GST/withholding by default? We need explicit language to map our tax codes.
- Our AP also needs a sample invoice (line items and tax breakdown) if you invoice before we issue the PO. Can you share a stub?

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick reply while we loop in Legal: 

1) Invoice triggers (proposed matrix attached):
   - Activation (one-time onboarding fee) -> invoice on activation completion (invoice A)
   - Minimum commit installments -> invoiced at start of each committed period or on calendar monthly pro rata if not tranching
   - Milestone billing (if customer requests tranche draws) -> invoice when milestone is accepted by both parties
   - Ad-hoc overage usage -> invoiced monthly with usage statement

   Fallback: if no PO is in place and customer requests invoicing, we will invoice per the triggers above; payment terms still governed by agreed Net Terms in the order form.

2) Tax responsibility (default):
   - Redwood will typically remit VAT on services where Redwood is the supplier of record.
   - If SkyTech provides a valid tax exemption or reverse-charge certificate (e.g., EU VAT reverse charge), Redwood will shift tax responsibility to SkyTech as documented.
   - We can add explicit language: "Customer shall provide any tax certificates required to support reverse charge or exemption; absent such certificate, Redwood will apply local VAT/GST."

3) Sample invoice: attached an "invoice-trigger-matrix.xlsx" with a sample layout and suggested line items/tax rows.

Next steps: Kimberly, Ben — please confirm if the proposed default tax clause is acceptable or if Legal needs a different formulation. Elena — if Tim (legal) wants alternative wording, happy to iterate.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
